approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from scored survivors, fits a count-fingerprint Gaussian process only to the current session's accepted results, and plans two batches at a time. It compares a Thompson-sampling batch with bounded single-position alternatives. For each imagined first outcome it uses an analytic conditional-tail policy to choose the second batch, evaluates that choice with independent samples, and then executes the same saved policy after real feedback. Its second batch can currently buy only candidates saved from the first pool.
approach.novelty: Add a small, preconstructed offspring bank from every possible first-batch molecule. An offspring becomes available to the second batch only if its source survives the first feedback update, and the planner prices exactly that future option before making its first purchase. The new mechanism changes which future actions exist. Earlier experiments changed commitment alignment or tail integration while retaining the saved candidate set; no same-Parent sibling has tested this offspring support.

hypothesis: Extend the Parent's outcome-conditioned expected-maximum recourse with a frozen bounded one-step offspring bank whose future membership is qualified by the hypothetical or actual top64 survival of its first-stage source. Construct before labels, value under the exact accepted-data joint GP, and physically execute the identical source-qualified support and inherited analytic policy after real feedback. This new executable future action set may move bank-only purchases and full two-batch progress; greater modeled utility or pool size alone is not the hypothesis.

finding_summary.headline: Outcome-qualified offspring improved full two-batch progress and the code-Parent endpoint
finding_summary.insights:
The registered bounded-bank useful-transfer prediction is supported on this Search panel: new modeled options were physically purchased, learned from and reused, and full-panel progress increased. Of the 784 bank purchases, 153 beat their real source and 73 improved the incumbent; their recorded incumbent increments sum to 1.644921, and 538 were later used as breeding parents. There were also 560 negative source gains and 71 ties. These are realized paths, not a decomposition of the total score effect: changed first batches, bank exposure and later descendants evolve together. The borrowed observation-dependent decision principle operated in valuation and actual recourse, while the discrete bounded graph adaptation remains distinct from the paper's continuous one-shot optimizer and performance claims.

The Parent's average optimistic second-batch gain estimate reversed: the Child's average modeled gain is lower than realized gain. This is not evidence of accurate ranking. 76 second batches had positive modeled value but no real progress, and modeled versus realized B gains have a descriptive pooled rank correlation of -0.127. Within-session correlations are mixed: 10 positive and 5 negative. These are changing adaptive states, not a controlled comparison of unpurchased candidates; the pooled direction does not establish a general ranking failure. A better calibrated recourse valuation or ranking model is a relevant method-level alternative to test for the flat batches and calibration mismatch; its usefulness is untested.

Support expansion also did not broaden the aggregate accepted search: generic scaffolds fell from 1,188 to 1,109 and fragment-excluded within-session similarity rose from 0.29881 to 0.30947. Both size tails shrank, yet unusual attachments remain, compressed unsaturated small-ring exposure increased and no configurations were specified despite 2,300 products with potential tetrahedral centres. Local-environment-aware ring/linker proposals and configuration-aware graph edits could address these specific limitations, but chemical quality is not established by the endpoint gain. The wider rollout approach, mediation, transfer beyond this panel and independent reliability remain open.
finding_summary.results:
The bank was built in all 210 planning announcements and supplied 784 of the 2,100 real second-batch purchases across 203 decisions. All 110,880 planned outcome scenarios and 210 actual recourse decisions reproduced the saved support, survival rule, conditional law and ordered policy choices. Across all 420 adjacent windows, mean realized best-progress rose from 0.02337166 to 0.02430726 (delta +0.00093559; 9 favorable and 6 adverse task/seed cells), passing the registered strict-increase test. Late purchase gain rose from 0.83542 to 1.77727.

Mean first-batch gain fell from 0.01594896 to 0.01248511, while second-batch gain rose from 0.00799012 to 0.01221134. Zero-progress second batches fell from 135 to 99 out of 210, but zero-progress full windows rose from 126 to 127 out of 420, and flat committed pairs rose from 58 to 60 out of 210. Mean modeled second-batch gain fell to 0.00931362, below the realized 0.01221134; the Parent had modeled 0.01220112 against realized 0.00799012.

Final mean Top-1 increased from 0.55060773 to 0.56025800, a paired gain of +0.00965027, above the separate +0.002 target. All three seed-macro changes were positive, with 8 favorable and 7 adverse task/seed endpoints. The code Parent task-safety calculation passes. The formal Anchor remains 0.04677231 higher, and the criterion requiring it as code Parent is inapplicable. All 15 sessions supplied complete paid outcomes with no fallback, invalid or duplicate evaluator submissions.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich amide, amine and heterocycle families retain reactive attachments and unresolved stereochemistry despite smaller size tails
molecular.overall_character: All five objectives and frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2 were read, giving 15 complete Child/code-Parent trajectory pairs. The actual code Parent is n-e68846780093. context.comparison independently records child_complete=true and paired_complete=true; all requested trajectory paths exist, and every paired session has the same ten initial identities and scores. Each side contains 4,350 accepted optimizer products, excluding initial observations. These observations do not describe unpurchased internal proposals. The Child mainly produces medium-sized aromatic and heteroaromatic systems with amides, carbonyl heterocycles, ethers, halogens and amines, alongside saturated fused or bridged rings, nitrogen-rich macrocyclic or expanded rings, and occasional very large repeated heteroaryl assemblies. The median is 30 heavy atoms, four perceived rings and three aromatic rings on both sides. Ring-bearing products are 4,181 versus 4,110, and aromatic-atom-bearing products 4,063 versus 4,060. This agrees with the digest presence counters; those counters do not measure the fraction of atoms that are aromatic. Ring chemistry, heteroaromaticity and accessible amine environments are demonstrated capabilities. Both size tails persist: 162 Child products have at most five heavy atoms versus 217 in the Parent, and 183 have at least 50 versus 276. The full Child range is one to 120 heavy atoms, compared with one to 118. The 4,257 distinct accepted canonical identities across Child sessions include 1,761 nonempty typed Murcko scaffolds and 1,109 generic scaffolds; the Parent has 4,226 identities, 1,901 typed and 1,188 generic scaffolds. Mean within-session Morgan Tanimoto after excluding products with at most five heavy atoms is 0.3094694511553078 versus 0.29880548278176255. This is substantial constitutional variation with recurrent local families and modestly narrower exploration in aggregate, with different directions across sessions. Neither scaffold counts nor this similarity measure establish useful chemical diversity. Attachment concerns remain: N-halogen-bearing products are 763 versus 766, O-halogen-bearing products 58 versus 76, and peroxide-bearing products 59 versus 91. Single N-N bonds occur in 527 versus 310 products, and single N-O bonds in 389 versus 273; these latter motifs include legitimate chemistry and require local context. Products containing a perceived ring of at most four atoms with an aromatic or multiple ring bond are 898 versus 386. That is a structural review flag, not a strain-energy or instability measurement. No accepted optimizer SMILES on either side contains explicit atom or bond stereochemistry, and no assigned tetrahedral centre is detected. At least one unassigned potential tetrahedral centre occurs in 2,300 Child products versus 1,899 Parent products. The greater exposure to unspecified stereochemistry includes favorable molecules and cannot be read as stereochemical improvement. All structural counts use identical RDKit 2023.09.6 definitions on both sides, retain multiplicity across sessions, and are observational. Synthetic plausibility is questionable because ordinary constituent groups coexist with reactive attachments, compressed ring arrangements and unspecified configurations. No synthesis route, stability, toxicity, solution-state protonation, medicinal efficacy, mechanism activation or component contribution is established. The score associations below do not identify an unseen optimal pharmacophore or prove that removing a flagged group would improve an objective. Methods, all session summaries and source references are in policy/scratch/r0078-00-improve-L01/molecular/aggregate.json. Byte-identical copies of all Child trajectories are preserved inside the run; original absolute paths and matching original/copy SHA256s are in policy/scratch/r0078-00-improve-L01/molecular/provenance.json. Published Parent trajectories are the comparison authority. No other molecular comparator is asserted.

Seed 0 retains an N-sulfanyl amide; seed 1 favors an N-amino heteroaromatic nitrogen plus an N-halogenated amide; seed 2 combines an N-methylamino substituent and fluoromethyl ether with an N-fluoro amide. The median is 25 heavy atoms and three rings, matching the Parent; 828/870 products contain aromatic atoms. The range is one to 35 heavy atoms. method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
